cli.usage:
RosmarOps reads your AI agents' configuration on this computer and reports what they can reach. Read-only; nothing leaves this computer.

Usage: rosmarops <command> [flags]

Commands:
completeness.partial: reduces this exposure; other ways remain
completeness.radius_only: narrows where it can be reached from; does not remove it
confidence.high: confidence high: rests on documented behaviour
confidence.medium: confidence medium: one step depends on something RosmarOps cannot confirm at rest
console.config_accepted: Accepted as the new trusted configuration.
console.config_changed: RosmarOps configuration changed since the last run:
console.config_confirm: Did you make these changes yourself? (y/n):
console.config_rejected: Ignored. The report marks this change in red.
console.config_unconfirmed: No one confirmed these changes, so they are ignored and the report marks them in red.
console.summary: {status} Red: {red} · Yellow: {yellow}. Legacy checks — red: {legacy_red} · yellow: {legacy_yellow}.
coverage.none: Everything RosmarOps looks for was read.
finding.cred_in_git.title: Your {cred_label} is saved in git
finding.cred_in_git.what: This credential is stored in {count} git repositories, in the current files or in past commits.
finding.cred_in_git.why.local: No remote is declared, so it has probably not left this machine yet. A push would send it with the whole history.
finding.cred_in_git.why.remote: At least one of these repositories declares a remote. If it was pushed, the key has already left this machine, and only rotating it cuts that.
finding.cred_read_and_send.title: {agent} can read your {cred_label} and send it out without anyone approving
finding.cred_read_and_send.title.multi: {agent} can read your {cred_label} and send it out without anyone approving
finding.cred_read_and_send.what: {agent} can read this credential without asking you, and it has a way to send data out of your machine that no person approves.
finding.cred_read_and_send.what.multi: {agent} can read this credential without asking you, and each of them has a way to send data out of your machine that no person approves.
finding.cred_read_and_send.why: Anything that can steer {agent}, such as instructions hidden in a web page, an issue, a dependency or a file it reads, could get this credential out. What it opens is whatever {service_name} lets this key do.
finding.cred_read_and_send.why.multi: Anything that can steer {agent}, such as instructions hidden in a web page, an issue, a dependency or a file they read, could get this credential out. What it opens is whatever {service_name} lets this key do.
finding.cred_readable.title: {agent} can read your {cred_label} without asking
finding.cred_readable.what: {agent} can read this credential without asking you. RosmarOps found no way for it to send data out without a person approving that step.
finding.cred_readable.what.multi: {agent} can read this credential without asking you. RosmarOps found no way for them to send data out without a person approving that step.
finding.cred_readable.why: The credential is one approval away from leaving: a command you approve without reading closely can send it. What it opens is whatever {service_name} lets this key do.
finding.foreign_agent_config_writable.wh: {agent} can write {target_agent}'s configuration without asking you. {target_agent} loads it the next time it starts.

This is how one compromised agent compromises another. A line added to {target_agent}'s configuration can start a program or a tool server the next time {target_agent} runs, outside {agent}'s session and its checks, with no trace in the session that made the change.
finding.foreign_agent_instructions_writa: {agent} can write the instruction files that {target_agent} follows without asking you.
An agent obeys its instructions. Text planted there is followed by every later {target_agent} session as if you had written it.
finding.own_config_writable.title: {agent} can change its own permissions
finding.own_config_writable.what: {agent} can write its own configuration or hook files without asking you.
finding.own_config_writable.why: An agent that can edit its own permissions or hooks can remove every limit you set, for this session and the next ones.
finding.own_instructions_writable.title: {agent} can rewrite its own instructions
finding.own_instructions_writable.what: {agent} can write its own instruction files without asking you.
finding.own_instructions_writable.why: One session that goes wrong can leave instructions that every later session reads and follows.

html.gloss.agent.a: An AI program that works on your computer with your permissions: it reads files, runs commands and edits code. Claude Code, Cursor and Cline are agents.
html.gloss.auto.a: A Claude Code mode in which it asks you much less: reads and edits inside the project are approved on their own, and most other actions are decided by another AI model. Since version 2.1.283 it is the mode Claude Code starts in unless you choose another.
html.gloss.config.a: The file where an agent lists the extra tools it starts when it opens (MCP servers). Whoever can write to it can make the agent run a new program.
html.gloss.env.a: A file where a project keeps its keys and passwords so it can run. It usually stays out of git, but it is still on your disk, and any program that can read your files can read it.
html.gloss.master.a: The Supabase key meant only for servers (service_role): it bypasses all the security rules of your database. It should not be on your computer unless it is essential.
html.gloss.score.a: It starts at 100 and drops with each warning, more for the serious ones and for the ones reachable from more places. With any urgent warning it never goes above 49; with only warnings to review, never above 79. The method is public.
html.gloss.settings.a: Claude Code's settings file for your user. It decides what Claude Code can do without asking you.

unknown.auto_classifier_permits: Depends on auto mode's classifier allowing the step. The classifier is a model, not a person, and RosmarOps cannot predict its decision.
unknown.auto_mode_available: Assumes auto mode is available to your account and model; if it is not, {agent} starts in manual mode.
unknown.bash_tool_available: Assumes {agent} has its shell tool available in your sessions.
unknown.code_launcher_rule: Relies on a pre-approved rule that runs code, such as node -e or powershell -Command, which is as broad as an unrestricted shell.
unknown.config_file_protection_scope_unk: Cursor protects some configuration files from edits without approval but does not list which; assumes this file is not among them.
unknown.edit_rule_partial: A rule covers these files for the edit tools, but shell commands can still write them.
unknown.ide_run_mode_not_readable: Assumes {agent} uses Auto-review, the mode Cursor recommends. The mode you choose in its settings is not stored where RosmarOps can read it.
unknown.no_pretooluse_hook_blocks: Assumes no hook of yours blocks this action before it runs. RosmarOps does not run hooks to find out.
unknown.process_runs_as_user: Assumes {agent} runs as your user account, with your file permissions.
unknown.read_deny_partial: A rule covers this file for the file tools, but shell commands can still read it.
unknown.remote_visibility_unknown: Knows that a remote is declared, not whether it is public or whether these commits were pushed.
unknown.sandbox_platform_unknown: Cursor does not document how its sandbox works on Windows; assumes it behaves as documented for other systems.
unknown.shell_write_unchecked: Relies on shell commands, which can write anywhere your user can; RosmarOps cannot see which commands will run.
unknown.team_policy_unknown: Assumes no team policy from a Cursor admin dashboard overrides your local settings; RosmarOps cannot see it.
unknown.third_party_imports_setting_not_: Assumes Cursor's Third-Party Imports setting is on, as it is by default. The setting is not stored where RosmarOps can read it.
unknown.ui_mode_choice_unknown: Assumes you use the default mode. A mode you pick in the app or the IDE is not stored where RosmarOps can read it.
unknown.version_behaves_as_documented: Assumes your installed version of {agent} behaves as its documentation says.
